paper_metadata.title: Effect of sintering temperature on microstructure evolution and mechanical properties of Al0.5CoCrFeNi high entropy alloy prepared by Spark Plasma Sintering

This strengthening effect is primarily attributed to the reduction of residual porosity and enhanced densification at moderate temperatures, which improve the effective load-bearing cross-section.

In contrast, toughness improves monotonically with increasing temperature. This enhancement originates from the progressive increase of the ductile FCC phase and the concurrent suppression of brittle BCC phases, which facilitate plastic deformation and delay fracture.
The coexistence of FCC and BCC phases thus provides both plasticity and strengthening in the microstructure.
At this time, the dislocation strengthening mechanism (Taylor hardening) dominates the mechanical properties, and the high-entropy alloy exhibits high tensile strength (1022 MPa).
